subject: Staged rendezvous plan for private fleet upgrade — AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, acme-deploy-lead@acmehealth.com
Cc: netops-svc@edgecloud.io
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged rendezvous plan for private fleet upgrade — AcmeHealth

Team / Acme ops —

Following our alignment call, I put together a concise rendezvous-driven cutover plan for the private (VPC/on-prem) upgrade to runtime v2.3.1 for the AcmeHealth tenant. High level: small canary, rendezvous point for cross-team checks, staged rollouts across racks, and an explicit rollback ladder. Attachments: preflight-checklist.pdf + netplan-change-diff.txt + canary-schedule.csv.

Key pillars (tl;dr):
- Preflight (72/24/1h checks): infra health, disk, KV cache snapshot, config diff review.
- Rendezvous: a 20-minute gated sync (video + shared chat) before each tranche that asserts green metrics (P90 latency, token error rate, served success).
- Staggered tranches: Zone A (10% fleet) -> 30m stabilization -> Zone B (30%) -> 1h stabilization -> Zone C (remaining 60%).
- Canary gating: automatic rollback if any tranche breaches a threshold (P90 > 250ms OR request error rate delta > 0.8%).
- Rollback ladder: 1) Shelve new version on affected nodes, 2) Evacuate traffic to pinned model variant, 3) Drain and re-image if infra fault suspected.

Asks by Monday EOD:
1) Neha — confirm KV-cache snapshot approach and whether we should force a cold-start on canary nodes.
2) Marissa — confirm the exact maintenance windows you can commit to for Acme (we proposed 01:00–05:00 UTC).
3) Soojin — validate operator runbook steps for automatic vs manual rollback.
4) Acme — any blackout windows (payroll batches, backups) we should avoid?

I recommend we lock a 4-hour window but allow the rendezvous to abort early if metrics look good and we finish quicker. If any of you see a conflict with region/local ops, flag now.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: preflight-checklist.pdf (pdf, 430KB stub), netplan-change-diff.txt (text), canary-schedule.csv (csv)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-deploy-lead@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staged rendezvous plan for private fleet upgrade — AcmeHealth

Karthik —

Thanks for drafting. A couple of quick clarifications from infra side:

1) KV cache snapshot: we should take a consistent KV snapshot at T-1h for the canary nodes and tag it with the model build id. That lets us restore without global invalidation. For canaries I'd prefer NOT to force a full cold-start (warm caches reduce flakiness for latency tests) — we should warm a small subset with synthetic traffic first.

2) Netplan diff: I reviewed netplan-change-diff.txt — the only cross-rack route change is the BGP next-hop rewrite for the canary bridge. We'll need a rollback netplan that reinstates the previous BGP rules (I can author that).

3) Verification signals: add KV-hit-rate and model-serve-error-code(5xx/429) to the gating list — not just latency.

I can take point on the snapshot and rollback netplan fragment. Will follow up with the exact git commit id for the change.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

All —

Synthetizing ops constraints for Acme: they gave us the following preferred window options (they confirmed with their infra):
- Primary preferred: 03:00–07:00 UTC on Saturday 2026-06-05 (low traffic)
- Backup window: 00:00–04:00 UTC Sunday 2026-06-06

Canary sequencing (proposal to accept):
- Canary 1 (10%): 00:00–00:40 UTC — smoke + synthetic heat + 30m stabilization
- Canary 2 (30%): 00:40–02:00 UTC — expanded load + 1h stabilization
- Full (remaining 60%): 02:00–04:00 UTC — monitor 60m, then mark done.

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- Any increase in 4xx/5xx above baseline + >0.5% absolute OR
- P90 increase > 80ms sustained for >5m OR
- Any data-plane KV-inconsistency event flagged by KV checksum compare.

Rollback steps (operator checklist):
1) Shelve candidate model variant on affected nodes (take affected nodes out of LB).
2) Apply rollback netplan (Neha to provide).
3) Force traffic to pinned model variant for Acme (model pin: v2.2.9-pinned).
4) Run validation suite against pinned variant.
5) If infra faults suspected, re-image nodes and re-enroll.

Comms plan: during rendezvous we will have a short-form status line every 15 minutes in the shared chat and a >green / amber / red> status card. If we abort a tranche we enter a 30-minute cool-off for postmortem data capture.

I will own Canary 2 and the final gating call. Neha — please send the netplan rollback fragment by EOD Monday so I can bake it into the runbook.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff Technical Program Manager, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the thorough plan. A few items from Acme ops:
- We need to avoid any tranche that intersects our payroll batch (starts 02:30 UTC). Can you shift the full tranche to start at 03:00 UTC instead of 02:00? That would push the final check window to 05:00 UTC but keeps us clear.
- We confirm the primary window: Saturday 03:00–07:00 UTC. Backup still Sunday 00:00–04:00 UTC as Marissa listed.
- We accept the rollback criteria but request that you notify our compliance mailbox (ops@acmehealth.com) with a 5-minute SLA for status and the immediate initiation of the rollback ladder if we hit the top-level trigger.

If you can update the canary schedule (canary-schedule.csv) and rerun the gating thresholds with the shifted timing, we can lock the date.

Thanks —
L. Patel
